clue.text: Point out drunk has answer to clue

parts.note: high means drunk or intoxicated
in crossword jargon a light is the answer entered for a clue

explanation.surface: A tipsy solver proudly indicates that they have filled in an entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight something is to draw attention to it, a synonym of pointing it out.

clue.text: Third person, first crime

parts.note: he is a third-person singular pronoun
1st, written out as IST with the numeral 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson somehow slides into a confession of a criminal debut.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in the abbreviation 1st is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, especially a daring one, so it is a crime.

clue.text: Gallery items for sale for a time on TV

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
at an auction a lot is an item or batch offered for sale

explanation.surface: An art gallery's stock is up for auction, sold during a television slot.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GODS is the cheap upper balcony in a British theatre. The God slot is the British name for the airtime set aside for religious programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: The God slot is the part of the television schedule given over to religious broadcasting.

clue.text: Secure forward position

definitions.meaning: to fasten with a key, as a door
in rugby a ... is a forward in the second row of the scrum

explanation.walkthrough: A LOCK is a second-row forward in rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Lock is both a verb for fastening securely and the name of a forward position in rugby.

clue.text: Shot the most recent to have died

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Shot the most recent to have died (4,4)' parses as GO + NEWEST for GONE WEST, but the answer is held as the four letters GONE, half of the enumerated answer.

clue.text: Missing end of wild party in Seattle, drunkenly head for New York?

indicators.note: the shortened party sits inside the rearranged city name
staggering letters of the city name are jumbled as if by a drunk
the final letter of the party word is dropped

parts.note: a rave is a wild party

explanation.surface: A partygoer in Seattle, tipsy and leaving before the end, sets off for New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's drunk partygoer misleads: 'drunkenly' acts on Seattle alone, and 'head for New York?' is the definition, the question mark admitting New York is only one eastward destination.
explanation.definitionFit: New York lies east of Seattle, so heading there is travelling east; the question mark admits the example.

clue.text: Region that's weathered wrongdoing's changing hands

indicators.note: the right hand becomes the left: R for right is swapped for L for left

parts.note: crime is wrongdoing; the 's is the verb is

explanation.surface: A moralist notes that the misbehaviour of a district shifts as power passes to new owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' swaps R (right) for L (left) in CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A clime is a region considered in terms of its climate, so its weather is its defining feature.

clue.text: Arts society on the up, without operating a Mafia

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Arts society on the up, without operating a Mafia' parses as ARTS SOC outside (without) ON A, the whole then reversed by 'on the up'; the reversal indicator stands between pieces it turns, and the container form is refused as a reversal split while the charade form drops 'without'.
annotationWithheld.clue: Arts society on the up, without operating a Mafia

clue.text: Where mother's carried out routine

indicators.note: out signals the letters of routine being put out of order

explanation.surface: A mother's daily routine is followed by her baby before birth.
explanation.definitionFit: In utero is Latin for in the womb, the place where an unborn child is carried.

clue.text: Wrong one charged after execution of sex offence

indicators.note: the wrong and the charged particle come after the beheaded word
an execution beheads, so the first letter of sex is cut off

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
an ion is an electrically charged atom or particle

explanation.surface: A sex offender is charged after an execution, a grim legal tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execution of' beheads SEX to leave EX.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion, obtaining money by threats, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Crime scene? It's an adult shot to pieces

indicators.note: wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective surveys a crime scene where an adult has been gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is SCENE plus ITS AN ADULT, fifteen letters; 'Crime' at the start is the definition, not part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent assault is a sexual offence in law, so a specific crime.

clue.text: Square-rigger found where water flows round rolling hills

indicators.note: the tap goes round the rearranged hills

parts.note: a tap is where water comes out

indicators.note: rolling hills turn over, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailing vessel is spotted where a stream winds round undulating countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: A square-rigger is a ship with square sails on its masts; the surface makes it sound like a landscape feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall ship is a traditional large sailing ship, typically square-rigged, so a square-rigger.

clue.text: Beasts in tree sinned, we hear — nothing odd there

indicators.note: only the even letters are kept, every odd-placed letter being dropped

explanation.surface: Animals in a tree have apparently misbehaved, but rumour says nothing strange happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound signal, but it is fodder: keep letters 2, 4, 6 and so on of TREE SINNED WE HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer are hoofed animals, plural here like 'Beasts'.

clue.text: Ex-offender in York near roundabout

indicators.note: going round about shows the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former criminal lives in Yorkshire near a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Kray was one of the Kray twins, gangsters who ruled London's East End in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronnie Kray was a convicted London gangster, so a dead former offender.

clue.text: Tailed setter carrying gun (model 4E) — it's efficient

indicators.note: the shortened setter carries the gun inside
the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: Puck is the setter of this puzzle
rod is slang for a gun
Model T Ford, then IV for 4 in Roman numerals, then E

explanation.surface: A setter's tailored gun, a model with a technical designation, turns out to work well.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck is this puzzle's setter. The Model T was an early Ford car, and 4 is IV in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Productive means yielding good results, close to efficient.

clue.text: Spooners draught animal on which 'e learnt to draw a dray?

definitions.text: on which 'e learnt to draw a dray?

indicators.note: a Spoonerism swaps the opening sounds of two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a cart horse is a heavy horse used for pulling
a cart horse is a heavy horse used for pulling

explanation.surface: A heavy horse that pulls a brewer's wagon is somehow taught to draw.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts of CART HORSE gives HART CORSE; drop the H as a Cockney would (hence 'e for he) and it sounds like ART COURSE. A dray is a brewer's cart.
explanation.definitionFit: An art course is where someone learns to draw, with the pun on drawing a cart.

clue.text: Social worker holding work-out in Georgia's Buddhist temple

indicators.note: the ant holds everything else inside it

parts.note: an ant is a social insect, a worker in a colony

indicators.note: the jumbled work goes inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation of the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: worked out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A welfare officer helps a client exercise at a temple in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a job title, but it is an insect: ants are social and the workers do the labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Angkor Wat in Cambodia is a vast temple complex, Hindu in origin and later Buddhist.

clue.text: Knocked back most of one Mickey Finn here?

indicators.note: drunk down, and read backwards
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Mickey Mouse, the cartoon character
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone downs most of a spiked drink, a Mickey Finn, and wonders where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts MOUSE to MOUS, and 'Knocked back' turns it to SUOM. A Mickey Finn is a drugged drink; 'Finn' becomes part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Suomi is the Finnish name for Finland, the home of Finns.

clue.text: Mischievous child "borrowing" a Mini's locked up

indicators.note: the answer is shut away within the run of words

explanation.surface: A young rascal takes a Mini for a joyride, and it ends up impounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, a cheeky or impish young child.

clue.text: Doctor on BBC, not a lawman

indicators.note: in a down entry the doctor sits on top of the next piece

parts.note: MO is medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: not a says the BBC nickname is to be written without its letter a, which is dropped

parts.note: Auntie is the affectionate nickname of the BBC

explanation.surface: A TV doctor on the BBC insists that he is no policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes A from AUNTIE to leave UNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, so a law officer.

clue.text: Criminal interned, so no escaping or running away

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent, so the letters are rearranged
the letter is let out of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An offender has been locked up, so there is no chance of fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no escaping' removes N from INTERNED; the remaining ITERNED with SO is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion, especially from the army, is running away from one's post or duty.

clue.text: Record label's 'Head of Espionage' follows first off hit list

indicators.note: the record label piece follows the trimmed word
the first letter is taken off

parts.note: EMI is a record label, with the 's giving S

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A record company's spymaster is named after a chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' trims HIT to IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, which is to list.

clue.text: Luxury version of coupe chap's broken into

indicators.note: the man goes inside the rearranged car word
a version is an altered form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Len is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone's upmarket coupé has been burgled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coupe' in the surface is a car; here it is just fodder, and 'chap' is any man's name, LEN being a standard crossword choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth and luxury.

clue.text: Direction to tie up serial killer first

indicators.note: serial killer first tells us the killer's name leads, ahead of the turned tie

parts.note: Fred West was a notorious English serial killer

indicators.note: in a down entry, up reverses the word

parts.note: a tie in a match is a draw

explanation.surface: An order to bind a murderer before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across then down, so 'up' turns DRAW into WARD for the down part. FRED WEST killed at least twelve people in Gloucester.
explanation.definitionFit: Westward is a direction, towards the west.

clue.text: Corrupt it isn't!

definitions.meaning: a dialect contraction of it is not

explanation.definitionFit: Taint means to corrupt or sully, and t'ain't is a colloquial contraction of it isn't.

clue.text: See 10
See 21
Wee drunk at party in the middle of the road? I can prove innocence!

parts.note: wee is urine, water
tight means drunk

indicators.note: the party goes in the middle of the road number

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's main north-south road, written AI
Lib is short for Liberal, a political party

explanation.surface: A drunk relieves himself in the street at a party, then insists he did nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; its 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A watertight alibi is an excuse that conclusively shows someone was elsewhere, proving innocence.

clue.text: Very little support for driving to the city

parts.note: in golf a tee holds the ball for a drive
NY is New York, the city

explanation.surface: A traveller gets scant help on the road to the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny is an informal word for tiny, very little.

clue.text: Former patient takes small boy for a time, as appropriate

indicators.note: receives one piece in place of another
for means instead of here

parts.note: ex- means former
taken as written
Ed is a boy's name, shortened

explanation.surface: A one-time hospital patient takes a young lad in for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXPATIENT, ED replaces AT ('a' plus T for time).
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means convenient and appropriate for a purpose.
